hed: Challenger responses due 4 p.m. EDT Wednesday on USPS mail-ballot stay (26A305)
dek: Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson directed challengers to respond by 4 p.m. EDT Wednesday, Sept. 9, to the Justice Department’s emergency stay application 26A305 seeking to lift U.S. District Judge Indira Talwani’s Sept. 4 preliminary injunction blocking mandatory parts of the Postal Service’s Aug. 26 Ballot Mail for Federal Elections rule for the Nov. 3 midterms. DOJ withdrew earlier application 26A297 aimed at Talwani’s TRO and refiled against the PI, with Solicitor General D. John Sauer citing states already mailing ballots.
alt: Election worker in blue gloves holding a vote-by-mail envelope
byline: Event summary from public reporting and named outlets

cl.body: SCOTUSblog, NBC News, and the Supreme Court docket frame Wednesday’s 4 p.m. EDT response deadline on 26A305 after Talwani’s PI blocked mandatory USPS election-mail rules.

cr.body: Washington Examiner, Fox News, and the DOJ stay application stress a push to enforce mail-ballot envelope and barcode rules before more states mail, with replies due Wednesday afternoon.

stack_blurb: Jackson set 4 p.m. EDT Sept. 9 replies on DOJ stay app.
seo_description: Justice Jackson ordered challenger responses by 4 p.m. EDT Sept. 9 to the USPS/DOJ stay application 26A305 after Judge Talwani’s preliminary injunction.
